about: The area config for one study round over the bot's loop (#8005 slice 5; docs/IA.md §5.2: is a bot running, what it decided, what it is subscribed to, its owner's switch — on /u/<bot> and the account's Playbooks and Thesis sections). Read by scripts/study/round.mjs; everything area-specific lives here or in scripts/study/worlds/bot-loop-*. Worlds: bot-loop-today (Sauron running and trading on its own, its wheel pointed at a conviction view that holds it; the friend's Day Trader held by its breaker) and bot-loop-steered (the same day with each owner steering: Sauron holding new positions, the Day Trader watching only). Viewers: eric owns Sauron, jordan owns The Day Trader, casey owns nothing. `roles` is who each member is here, in plain words, read by the experts and the words pass instead of the cards (#5099), so it never quotes a card. Census routes are copied from links the app builds (a Ledger row's playbook link, a position's Trade link, the Playbooks section's way to R&D, the league card's leaderboard), never composed. No sealed key, framer or tasks yet: those come when the cross-feature round clears (#8005). Run 2026-11-23 (surge, the reset at 05:00Z): every census at phone width only, so the experts review the phone, where members struggle (study lesson 2026-10-09); the members still run desktop where the matrix says. The friend owner view is reviewed by the experts once, in the steered world, not twice (budget ~830 calls). CONTROL copy: the census narrows to the two owner views where every fixed and planted mechanism lives (Sauron owner pages, R&D and Settings; the watching Day Trader), phone only; everything the questions depend on is the main round's.

matrix.note: owns the bot its breaker holds, and reads the other bot as a member, not its owner
their own bot set to watch only since Friday
owns nothing; starts where the league card's link lands

roles.eric: Runs the league and owns one of its two bots, which places paper orders by itself; wants to know whether it is working, what it did and what is holding it back. On a phone when away, at a desk at home.
roles.invited-friend: A friend the owner invited, a member and not the owner, who has a small account of their own and a bot they took over; wants to know whether their bot is working and what they can do about it. Mostly on a phone.
roles.bot-watcher: Owns no account at all; keeps up with the league's bots the way a fan keeps up with a team, and reads what each one did and why. On a phone.
roles.phone-only: Owns one of the league's bots and only ever checks on it from a phone, one-handed, in short visits.

pages: a bot account's own public page: whether it is running, what it holds, and where it stands in the league
the bot's checks of the market: when it last checked, whether anything is holding it back, and one card per strategy it runs with what each is doing
every check the bot recorded, including the ones held back or refused
the bot's history of orders, newest first, each with why it was placed and which strategy placed it
how the bot's money has moved over time: its equity curve, streaks and results by week
the bot's reasoning: its view of the market, its trades drawn on a chart, and the safety stages that protect each strategy
the same checks and reasoning as sections of the owner's own accounts overview
the owner's settings for a bot: pausing it, holding back new positions, watching only, re-arming a safety stop, and a log of every change
the strategy catalog where an owner subscribes a bot to strategies, and to a dated view of the market that narrows one
where these pages send you next: the league table, the trade screen for one holding, and the strategy catalog
